comparison: Both address Model A2 behavior (C57, C58, C60, C61). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by simulation data in Figures 2I-J and 3C-D with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting that Model A2 lacks sufficient explanation and requesting either supplemental placement or clearer presentation.

Both address the evolutionary trajectory from sizers to adders (C62, C86-C92). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by detailed analysis in Figure 5 showing the two-step pathway and inverse correlation. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether the distinction relates to steady-state CV_birth versus perturbation recovery and requesting mechanistic clarification.

Both address mouse epidermal stem cell context and G1 phase dominance (C72-C76). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by simulation data in Figures 4C-D with statistical analysis (p=4×10⁻³ and p<10⁻⁴) and appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, with no direct challenges to the experimental citations or biological context.

Both address evolutionary algorithm methodology (C21, C22, C129). OpenEval finds the methodological rationale SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to prior work. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting clarification of how the evolutionary approach differs from other approaches and asking for comparison with existing mathematical methods.

Both address cell cycle parameter variation effects (C28-C30, C77-C84). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by systematic simulation experiments in Figures 4 and Appendix figures 5-7. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about robustness, questioning whether findings hold with different numbers of simulations and epochs, and whether parameter choices were arbitrary.

Both address fluctuation-sensing networks and SOC (C100, C101, C107-C109, C111, C115, C119). OpenEval finds most claims SUPPORTED but notes UNCERTAINTY about SOC characterization strength. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, stating Figures 6H-J are 'not very clear' with insufficient captions, raising questions about evidence supporting SOC claims.

Both address self-organized criticality claims (C111, C115, C119, C136, C137). OpenEval expresses UNCERTAINTY about the 'first example' claim and statistical robustness of SOC characterization, noting limited power-law fit data. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY due to unclear presentation of supporting figures, making it difficult to evaluate the strength of SOC evidence.

Both address S. pombe comparison and cell cycle structure influence (C69-C71, with peer also including C7, C31). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by simulation data with statistical analysis (p=0.03). Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, with no direct challenges to the findings, though they request broader validation with other real-life analogies.

Both address noise effects on size control (C79-C81). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by Appendix figures and appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, raising no specific concerns about the noise analysis results.

Both address the surprising finding that adders evolve more frequently (C62, C63). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by data in Figure 4, with the surprise justified by theoretical understanding. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning the underlying mechanisms and requesting clarification about steady-state versus perturbation dynamics.

Both address the adder prevalence finding (C62). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by simulation data. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting statistical summaries and clarification about network topology consistency and CV_birth ranges, indicating concerns about robustness and generalizability.

Both address stochastic nature of evolution and variability (C35, C123). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as appropriate caveats about non-determinism. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, implicitly acknowledging variability through their requests for robustness characterization and statistical summaries.

Both address Mixed Feedback Loop topology and titration mechanism (C26, C27). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by simulation data in Figures 2 and 5. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting statistical summaries and clarification about whether all simulations resulted in topologically similar networks and whether molecular details affect outcomes.

Both address main conclusions about cell cycle structure influence (C7, C70). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as well-justified general principles from comprehensive simulation results. Peer reviewers find these SUPPORTED with no direct challenges, though they request broader validation beyond the S. pombe comparison.

Both address homeostatic control (C55). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by simulation data in Figures 2I-J. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY due to lack of statistical summaries for Figures 2 and 3, making it difficult to assess robustness of homeostatic control claims.

Both address homeostatic control (C51). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by demonstration in Figure 2F. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting absence of statistical summaries and requesting information about CV_birth ranges and molecular implementation effects on outcomes.

Both address the general principle about cell cycle structure (C133). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as a synthesis of major findings. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether this principle explains why late cycle control favors sizers and requesting more mechanistic explanation.

Both address comparison with analytical methods (C129). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as appropriate positioning of the work. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting clarification of how the evolutionary approach differs from other approaches and asking for comparison with existing mathematical methods.

OpenEval finds background knowledge claims (C1-C4, C10-C20, C23-C25) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/introduction claims.

OpenEval finds summary statements about contributions (C8, C34-C36) SUPPORTED, appropriately positioning the work and acknowledging stochastic nature. Peer reviewers address C34 and C35 separately in other results but do not provide a unified evaluation of these summary claims.

OpenEval finds methodological considerations and limitations (C123-C130, C132) SUPPORTED as appropriate discussion. Peer reviewers address C123, C129, and C35 in separate results but do not provide comprehensive evaluation of all methodological discussion claims together.
